pick.headline: M-19 guerrillas seize Dominican Embassy in Bogota
pick.summary: On February 27, 1980, M-19 guerrillas seized the Dominican Republic's embassy in Bogota during a reception, taking about sixty hostages including the US ambassador.
pick.significance: The siege lasted 61 days and ended with the guerrillas flying to Cuba with some hostages, who were then freed.
pick.fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of February 28, 1980, carried live Bogota radio coverage: about two dozen heavily armed guerrillas stormed the Dominican embassy during its national day reception, taking the diplomatic corps hostage and wounding U.S. Ambassador Asencio, with radio first naming the Workers' Self-Defense Movement.

alternates.headline: Anti-Armenian pogrom in Sumgait
alternates.summary: On February 27, 1988, mobs began attacking Armenians in Sumgait, Azerbaijan; Soviet troops restored order after three days of violence.
alternates.significance: The pogrom, a week after the Karabakh vote, made the Armenian-Azerbaijani conflict violent.
alternates.fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of March 1, 1988, carried a terse Moscow TASS item that "a group of hooligans" provoked disturbances in Sumgait on February 28, followed by "rampage and violence", and that order was being restored, next to Yerevan radio on party secretaries touring a plant.

alternates.headline: Bush halts the Gulf War
alternates.summary: On the evening of February 27, 1991, President Bush announced that Kuwait was liberated and offensive operations would be suspended.
alternates.significance: The cease-fire left Saddam Hussein in power, with consequences for the uprisings that followed in Iraq.
